To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
influenza virus proteins can be synthesized in a wheat embryo translation system.
the influenza virus proteins are made in a cell-free system and the NS1 and NS2 proteins can be distinguished by the use of a cell-free system.

the in vitro translation of the influenza virus messenger RN As resulted in the production of the P1 and P 2 polypeptides, the nucleoproteins NP, the matrix proteins M, and the NS 1 nonstructural proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of the influenza virus proteins in vitro.
the synthesis of proteins by the influenza virus in vitro.

the development of a cell-free system for the synthesis of influenza virus proteins and the use of this system to determine whether the nonstructural protein (NS1) is a precursor of the matrix protein (M).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the wheat embryo translation system is a good in vitro system for studying the synthesis of the influenza virus proteins.
the in vitro system described in this report is useful for the study of translation of influenza virus RNAs.
the in vitro system is useful in studying the translation of influenza viral messenger RNAs and the products formed, but that it cannot be used as an assay for the glycosylation of viral proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in vitro translation of influenza A virus messenger RNAs is possible but that glycosylation of viral proteins is not.
the wheat embryo translation system can be used to study influenza virus messenger RNA translation but it cannot be used to study glycosylated influenza virus protein synthesis.
influenza virus messenger RN As are efficiently translated in vitro, but glycosylation of the viral proteins does not occur.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the in vitro system is useful for analyzing influenza virus proteins and that it can be used to analyze other viruses as well.
the in vitro translation system was able to translate influenza virus mRNA into proteins, and this system can be used to study the regulation of influenza virus mRNA translation.
the influenza virus messenger RNA translation system in wheat embryo is very similar to that in mammalian cells.
